scout.fields.description: Comma-separated top-level field names to return per row (e.g. fields=name,slug,tvlUSD), shrinking the payload. Case-insensitive. Each row's identity keys (id/slug/fullName/githubUsername/url/source, where present) are always included; unknown names are ignored, not rejected. Applies only to the rows array: meta is unaffected. Nested objects are selected whole (no dot-paths).
scout.fields.name: fields

scout.limit.description: Max results per page. The default and cap VARY by endpoint (e.g. projects/search 20/100, builders 50/200, leaderboard 50/300, research 8/25). A value below 1 or above the cap is clamped, not rejected.
scout.limit.name: limit

scout.offset.description: Number of matching rows to skip before returning (pagination). Page until offset + meta.counts.returned >= meta.counts.total.
scout.offset.name: offset

scout.view.description: Row shape. `full` (the default) returns every row field, unchanged. `compact` is for callers whose tool output is capped: each row is rebuilt from a fixed key list (identity, rank and score, and the fields that answer the usual question), and list fields left out come back as counts. A default projects/search page for q=lending measured 87,157 characters full and 23,091 compact (2026-10-23). Every compact row carries the same keys, null where there is no value; a field missing from a compact row was left out, not found empty. `meta.view` (first in meta) says the page is compact and where the left-out detail is read: repeat the request without view, or without view and with fields=<names>. The key lists are in the CompactView schema. Cannot be combined with fields (400). Any other value answers 400 with validValues.
scout.view.name: view

scout.RequestError.description: The request itself was wrong (a 400): fix the call, do not retry it as is.

scout.RetryableError.description: A failure the caller should retry: the read behind the answer failed (database, upstream, or this instance's rate window). Never a claim about the data; `advisory` says what the failure is NOT a claim about. Mirrors the Retry-After header in seconds.

advisory.description: What the failure is not a claim about, and what to do (retry after Retry-After, or where else to look).

hint.description: On a 429: the wait and the next step in words, the same number as retryAfterSeconds ('Wait 37 seconds, then resend the same request.'), for a consumer that keeps only error and hint.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Seconds to wait before resending; the same value as the Retry-After header. On a 429, the seconds until the rate window resets, or the language model's own wait (at most 3600, 60 when it sent no usable number); on a 503, 2 on database reads and 60 or 300 on the skills registry.

apiVersion.description: API contract (OpenAPI) version: equals /api/openapi.json info.version. Reason about the live contract from this rather than the service version.

count.description: null = the source could not be read with this response (could not check), never zero.

indexBytes.description: hackathonBuilds only: the serialised size in bytes of the hackathon submissions index, as its last build on the server instance answering measured it (lastUpdatedAt dates it). Next caches the index as one item of at most 2 MB; past that every request rebuilds it from the store, so a live check reds above 1,800,000. null = that instance has not built the index yet (could not check). Absent on every other source.

populationId.description: Scope digest of what `count` counts: same format as meta.population.id on /api/analyze and /api/clusters. DB-backed sources here are `<collection>|status:all` (the FULL collection incl. Inactive), which is why projects.count is larger than analyze/clusters' active-only populations. Different ids = different populations: never merge or compare the numbers without labeling the scopes.

info.description: One spec covering every operation this MCP server can execute, across four services: lumenloop, scout (Stellar Light), stellarDocs (Mintlify-backed docs search), and skills (pinned agent playbooks). Paths are keyed '/{service}/{operation}' and each operationId is the exact callable name: an operation with operationId 'lumenloop.search_directory' is invoked inside the execute tool's sandbox as `await lumenloop.search_directory(args)` — args is ONE object matching the operation's requestBody schema (POST ops) or its parameter names (GET ops). The exact call line is on each operation as x-execute. Every call resolves (never throws) to { ok: true, data, asOf, asOfBasis, caveat? } or { ok: false, error: { service, kind, message } }; the 200 response schema documents `data`. `asOf` is the upstream data date (dataAsOf or asOf) when the payload states one, else the host observation time, and `asOfBasis` names which; `caveat` is "no-rows" or "unverified-match" when the host can show it. Every path in this spec is callable — exposure is filtered at build time, so nothing uncallable is described. Auth is handled host-side — code never sees keys.

constraints.pagePaths: The page endpoint takes the path without a leading slash and returns 404 { message: "Page not found" } for an unknown path.
constraints.resultShape: Search returns an array of { path, content, metadata: { title } }: one entry per section chunk, no score, no anchor, no total count. A page can appear more than once.

backend.retry: one host; retry once on network error, timeout, or HTTP 5xx; never retry 4xx; 429 returns immediately
